newsitem.title: USA: Intel posts sharp profit, sales gains in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Intel posts sharp profit, sales gains in quarter.

text.p: Intel Corp. Monday said profits jumped 40 percent in the third quarter, reflecting solid demand for its Pentium computer chips and exceeding expectations on Wall Street.
The world's largest chip maker said it earned $1.3 billion in the quarter ended in September, up from $931 million in the 1995 quarter. Revenues rose 23 percent to $5.14 billion.

The profits, which equalled $1.48 a share, easily surpassed Wall Street's consensus estimate of $1.25, sending Intel's shares sharply higher in after-hours trading. In the year-ago quarter, Intel earned $1.05 a share, including an a one-time gain of 3 cents per share.
Traders said Intel rose $6.875 to $114.50 from its earlier close of $107.625 on Nasdaq.

"We are delighted with the excellent acceptance of Pentium and Pentium Pro processor-based PCs and servers, which has produced a stronger third quarter than we had originally expected," Intel President Andrew Grove said in a statement.

The company said unit shipments of microprocessors and chipsets set records in the quarter. But other products, including flash memory chips, were slightly down in unit volumes from the second quarter.
Intel has benefited from the strong acceptance of its Pentium and Pentium Pro microprocessors -- the powerful chips that allow users to operate various programmes at the same time.
Intel said its Pentium Pro processor continued to gain rapid market acceptance.
Revenue for the first nine months of 1996 rose 24 percent to $14.41 billion from $11.62 billion a year ago, and net income grew 20 percent to $3.25 billion from $2.70 billion.
Earnings per share grew to $3.67 from $3.06.
